data.hypothesis: The catalog has seven distinct valid programs; unaligned SIMD measured 0.079892 s, runtime-peeled 16-byte SIMD measured 0.079254 s, and the 32-byte alignment variant measured 0.080007 s, while 64-byte alignment was slower at 0.087704 s. This candidate tests a different factor: guarded OpenMP SIMD with simdlen(4), without an alignment claim or peel, to see whether limiting concurrent x iterations improves the frozen compiler's lowering. These prior measurements do not predict this candidate's outcome.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this stencil's independent cell updates and contiguous x traversal, compare SIMD-width choices separately from alignment handling; retain the scalar fallback and verify the interior offset in official correctness tests.
memory_lessons.claim: Measured guarded SIMD variants clustered near 0.079-0.080 s, while the runtime-peeled 64-byte alignment variant measured 0.087704 s. The small differences among the faster variants do not establish a stable alignment benefit.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this guarded simdlen(4) candidate under the official protocol and compare it with unaligned default-width SIMD and runtime-peeled 16-byte SIMD.

data.notes: The edit only adds a guarded simdlen(4) directive to the existing contiguous-x loop. It makes no alignment assumption, so the interior start at x0 remains valid for aligned or unaligned row addresses. The timestep kernel remains unfused; threading and spatial or temporal blocking are unchanged. No local commands, correctness validation, or performance measurements were run; the controller should validate and measure under the official settings.
transformations: Keep the unfused single-timestep stencil, arithmetic order, and existing interior bounds unchanged.
Guard an OpenMP simdlen(4) directive on the contiguous x-loop with the OpenMP 4.0 version check; compile the same scalar loop otherwise.
Make no alignment claim or scalar-peeling assumption, preserving correctness when the interior begins at a non-aligned offset.
Do not alter compiler flags, threading, spatial blocking, or temporal blocking.
